legend: Adenocarcinoma NOS ex intraductal carcinoma. Adjacent to an intercalated duct–type intraductal carcinoma (left), there is a frankly infiltrative tumour (right) comprising irregular glands and micropapillae. Both components harboured NCOA4::RET.

Adenocarcinoma NOS, low-grade. This oral cavity tumour was made up of solid nests punctuated by ducts lined by monotonous round nuclei. It does not conform to any known tumour type and was negative for fusions by RNA sequencing.

Adenocarcinoma NOS, intermediate-grade. This submandibular gland tumour consisted of one cell type with monotonous dark nuclei, arranged as infiltrative solid and cribriform nests, cords, and ducts in a myxoid stroma. The tumour was negative for fusions by RNA sequencing.

Adenocarcinoma NOS, high-grade. This submandibular gland tumour has irregular ducts lined by pleomorphic cells with necrosis and a high mitotic rate. There are no overtly apocrine features, and AR (not shown) was negative.

Adenocarcinoma NOS, high-grade. This submandibular gland tumour is highly invasive, with a desmoplastic stroma and perineural spread. The tumour grows as cords and ducts lined by pleomorphic cells with a high mitotic rate. Necrosis is identified. Foci of hyalinization raise the possibility of a prior pleomorphic adenoma, but no obvious benign elements were identified and no fusions were found by RNA sequencing. The tumour lacks apocrine morphology and was negative for AR (not shown). It is best regarded as high-grade adenocarcinoma NOS, a diagnosis of exclusion.
